change.author: Sam Jewell

findings.title: enableSqlExpressions ignores the feature flag; both branches return false
findings.body: `enableSqlExpressions` reads `FlagSqlExpressions`, negates it, and then returns `false` on both branches. So the flag lookup does nothing, and the name suggests a toggle check that never happens. If the goal is to switch SQL expressions off unconditionally (as the PR body says), drop the helper and return the error directly in `case QueryTypeSQL`, with a comment pointing to the DuckDB removal. If the goal is to honour the flag, the function should be `return h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)`. With the code as written, the next reader can't tell which one was meant.

findings.title: Legacy (non-expressionParser) path reports disabled SQL expressions as invalid SQL
findings.body: Only the `expressionParser` path (`pkg/expr/nodes.go:123-146` → `ReadQuery`) gets the new "sqlExpressions is not implemented" error. The default path, `buildCMDNode` → `UnmarshalSQLCommand` (`pkg/expr/nodes.go:159-160`) → `NewSQLCommand` → `sql.TablesList`, has no gate. `TablesList` now calls the stub `RunCommands`, which always returns "not implemented" (`pkg/expr/sql/db.go:16-18`). That logs `error serializing sql` at Error level, and `NewSQLCommand` turns it into the public BadRequest `sql-invalid-sql` / "error reading SQL command" (`pkg/expr/sql_command.go:30-35`). A user with a saved SQL expression is told their SQL is wrong, not that the feature is disabled, and every evaluation writes an error log line plus a warning. Consider returning a dedicated "SQL expressions are not supported" error early in `NewSQLCommand` (or `UnmarshalSQLCommand`) so both paths behave the same.

findings.title: Unused DB.TablesList stub and stale DuckDB naming
findings.body: Nothing calls `(*DB).TablesList`: all callers use the package-level `sql.TablesList` in parser.go. The stub can go. `parser.go:23` still names the variable `duckDB` and still builds a DuckDB-only `json_serialize_sql` command that can never run now. A short comment on `DB` saying it is a placeholder after removing go-duck would make the stub's purpose clear.

contracts.action: SQL expression parsed via ExpressionQueryReader (expressionParser flag on)
contracts.before_after: Before: parsed SQLExpression and built SQLCommand via DuckDB TablesList. After: always returns error 'sqlExpressions is not implemented' before reading the body, since enableSqlExpressions always returns false.
contracts.visible_effect: buildCMDNode returns the error (nodes.go:141-143); the query request fails with that message.
contracts.failure_mode: Always fails, and visibly; the feature flag has no effect.

contracts.action: SQL expression parsed via legacy path (expressionParser flag off)
contracts.equivalent_path: ReadQuery SQL case gate in pkg/expr/reader.go:129-132
contracts.before_after: Before: TablesList ran DuckDB json_serialize_sql. After: RunCommands stub returns 'not implemented'; TablesList logs Error and returns error; NewSQLCommand returns BadRequest sql-invalid-sql.
contracts.visible_effect: User sees public message 'error reading SQL command' (pkg/expr/sql_command.go:33-35).
contracts.failure_mode: Visible error, but it is misleading: it says the SQL is invalid, not that the feature is disabled.

contracts.before_after: Now always returns error, which is put in rsp.Error. In practice it can't be reached, because NewSQLCommand already fails at TablesList.
contracts.visible_effect: If it were ever reached, the node result would carry error 'not implemented'.
contracts.failure_mode: Error is surfaced through rsp.Error, not dropped silently.

summary: The PR removes the go-duck dependency, puts stubs that always return "not implemented" in its place, and makes the expressionParser reader reject SQL expressions. I found no blockers. The dependency file changes are consistent: hashes moved from go.sum to go.work.sum. Three findings, all at "consider": (1) `enableSqlExpressions` reads the feature flag but returns false on both branches, so the check does nothing and the intent is unclear. (2) The legacy, non-expressionParser path has no gate, so a disabled SQL expression shows the misleading BadRequest "error reading SQL command" and writes an Error log line every time. (3) `DB.TablesList` is an unused stub, and DuckDB naming is left over in parser.go.
